evidence_set: eFigure 5 plots, for each group, the adjusted mean daily probability of a self-reported nonfatal overdose across the 28-day observation period against age, on a log scale; the article's Results say the association was modified by age in adjusted but not in unadjusted analyses, and give no age-specific ratios. Editors' reading of the figure (measured from the image): the probabilities are drawn with 95% bands over ages 19 to 76; the strip group's line falls steeply with age while the comparison group's stays nearly flat, the two crossing at about age 42, so the modelled risk is higher in the strip group among younger and lower among older participants; the two bands overlap at every age; the plotted probabilities (about 0.0003 to 0.014 in the strip group and 0.002 to 0.003 in the comparison group) are well below the mean daily risk of 0.02 in the article's Results, so they were computed at covariate values the figure does not state.
